slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Exod 33:19: I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.
slides.body: “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.”
slides.heading: Exod 33:19

slides.body: God tells Moses he will show mercy and compassion. Luke later says mercy will be shown to Israel's fathers as Davidic salvation arrives.
slides.heading: Mercy foretold?

slides.body: Luke's hymn speaks of a Davidic horn of salvation. A commentator reads its mercy as salvation by Christ: a meaningful theological connection.
slides.heading: Christ brings God's mercy

slides.alt_text: Slide 3: The grammatical and direct-citation evidence.
slides.body: God speaks in Exodus and is the one showing mercy in Luke. Romans quotes Exodus as God's own words. Jesus may mediate mercy, but this pair is not a Jesus-character forecast.
slides.heading: Check the speaker
